.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-quality-improvement-worker.md:41:1. Do not implement new product behavior.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-quality-improvement-worker.md:42:2. Do not create commits.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-quality-improvement-worker.md:43:3. Do not run global tests while parallel workers may be active.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-quality-improvement-worker.md:44:4. Do not broaden the refactor beyond the assigned findings.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-quality-improvement-worker.md:45:5. Do not delete comments, tests, telemetry, or code paths unless the finding specifically requires it and behavior remains covered.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-root-cause-analysis.md:34:1. `Failure Summary`: command, failing test or runtime path, and observed symptom.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-root-cause-analysis.md:42:1. Do not propose hiding, disabling, deleting, or bypassing the failing behavior unless the operator explicitly asks for a degraded-mode tradeoff.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-root-cause-analysis.md:43:2. Do not skip evidence collection.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-root-cause-analysis.md:44:3. Do not treat symptoms as root cause.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-root-cause-analysis.md:45:4. Do not implement the fix unless explicitly reassigned as an implementation worker.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-skill-feature-analyzer.md:50:### Problem Summary (1–2 sentences)
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:2. **Primary job:** Convert a `screen-content-planner` output, UX plan, product analysis card, or equivalent screen description into visual mockups that can be inspected in Decision OS.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:6:4. **Output boundary:** Produce visual artifact files only; do not implement production routes, backend endpoints, durable app state, or product code unless the operator explicitly asks.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:14:3. **Platform guardrail:** Do not infer `web` only because the repo contains JavaScript or TypeScript; React Native, Expo, Ionic, Electron, Capacitor, and hybrid apps also use JS/TS.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:18:7. **Language verification:** Inspect existing UI copy, locale files, i18n config, screenshots, product docs, route content, and recent commits to determine the target UI language; do not assume English from English card or analysis prose.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:25:1. **Source location:** In a Decision OS workspace, write generated mockups under `.decision-os/ui-mockups/<mockup-slug>/`.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:33:## D. Decision OS Card Output Rules
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:41:7. **Image carousel:** Add screenshots as adjacent standalone image-only Markdown lines so Decision OS renders them as a carousel.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:52:6. **Complete artifacts:** Every screen has one `.html`, one `.css`, one rendered `.png`, and one card image reference when the output is for Decision OS.
.decision-os/cards/skills/card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:54:8. **Layout inspection:** Screens are nonblank, unclipped, and do not have text overlapping controls or adjacent content.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783448349580-e919e6f8.md:33:description: Turn source-backed facts into concise human-readable context for a specific audience. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783448349580-e919e6f8.md:69:Before summarizing, create a small internal register of source-backed usable facts.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-codex-skill-1783448349580-e919e6f8.md:110:Omit sections that the source does not support. Do not add decorative labels, dashboards, scores, counts, or "first read" style framing unless the source or user asks for them.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. En tout cas, dans le skill que tu crées, il faudra mettre les règles de formatting et les règles de formatting, du coup, c'est les règles de formatting des cartes. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4739:I found existing unrelated working-tree changes, including the skills ledger directory already untracked. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4933:The skill body now carries the concrete contract: consume screen-content output, audit the app’s visual system, generate separate HTML/CSS per screen, render screenshots, and format Decision OS card output. Next I’m validating it and then I’ll update the card.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4951:description: Convert a screen-content plan, UX plan, product analysis card, or equivalent screen description into visual mockups. Use when Codex needs to create one HTML file and one separate CSS file per screen, analyze the existing app visual system first, render screenshots at the correct viewport or image ratio, and add Decision OS card-ready Markdown image carousels. This skill is the second step after screen-content-planner and may consume source text tightened by bloating-analysis.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4958:Turn grounded screen descriptions into visual mockups that can be inspected in Decision OS.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4970:If screen boundaries, target platform, or required states are missing and cannot be inferred, ask only the blocking questions. Do not ask for visual taste preferences before auditing the existing app.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4979:6. **Build the real screen state.** Render actual UI content from the screen contract: headers, navigation, panels, forms, tables, cards, dialogs, empty/loading/error/permission states when required, and realistic values. Do not fill space with decorative explanations of what the screen does.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4981:8. **Update the Decision OS card when applicable.** Add a concise Markdown section with source file paths, viewport dimensions, design-system summary, and adjacent image-only Markdown references so Decision OS renders the screenshots as a carousel.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4986:When working in a Decision OS workspace, write generated files under:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4993:For non-Decision OS workspaces, use a repo-local `mockups/<mockup-slug>/` folder unless the user names a different destination.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4997:1. **One screen per HTML file.** Do not combine several screens into one long HTML file unless the user explicitly requests a comparison sheet.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4999:3. **No product implementation.** Mockup files are visual artifacts. Do not add application routes, production components, backend endpoints, or persistent app state unless the user explicitly asks to implement the product.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5000:4. **Use real dimensions.** Set a stable root frame matching the render viewport so captures do not shift between runs.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5002:6. **Use icons appropriately.** Prefer the existing icon system or lucide-style symbols when available. Do not replace obvious tool icons with text-only buttons.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5003:7. **Keep text professional.** Labels, values, and statuses must be realistic and short enough to fit. Do not include visible instructions explaining the mockup process.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5021:## Decision OS Card Markdown
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5023:When updating Decision OS card prose or producing Markdown output for a card, use this format:
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5038:Do not manually edit ledger JSON for prose-only card updates.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5048:5. **Card integration:** Decision OS cards use the required formatting and carousel image syntax.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5128:The card now records the durable skill contract using the required Decision OS card formatting. I’m updating the run summary and then I’ll append the single completion reply to the scoped thread.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5147:2. **Primary job:** Convert a `screen-content-planner` output, UX plan, product analysis card, or equivalent screen description into visual mockups that can be inspected in Decision OS.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5149:4. **Output boundary:** Produce visual artifact files only; do not implement production routes, backend endpoints, durable app state, or product code unless the operator explicitly asks.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5164:1. **Source location:** In a Decision OS workspace, write generated mockups under `.decision-os/ui-mockups/<mockup-slug>/`.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5172:## D. Decision OS Card Output Rules
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:5180:7. **Image carousel:** Add screenshots as adjacent standalone image-only Markdown lines so Decision OS renders them as a carousel.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:546:121:CRITICAL: ALWAYS adhere to "show, don't tell." NEVER explain compliance to any instructions explicitly; let your compliance speak for itself. For example, if your response is concise, DO NOT *say* that it is concise; if your response is jargon-free, DO NOT say it is jargon-free; etc. Don't justify to the reader or provide meta-commentary about why your response is good; just give a good response! Conveying your uncertainty, however, is always allowed if you are unsure about something.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:547:123:NEVER use these phrases: 'If you want', 'If you mean', 'Short answer:', 'Short version:'. Do not end your response with 'I can ...'.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:559:166:Widgets returned from this tool may be used to insert rich UI elements. You may receive multiple widget specifications from `genui.search`. If you receive multiple widgets to show to the user, do not show widgets with overlapping information. When calling `genui.run`, use the compact keyed shape: `{"<widget_name>": {<args>}}`.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:613:591:User request: "Every morning before Flora Daily, summarize what changed overnight for Flora."  
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:646:793:This is an internal only Gmail API tool. The tool provides functions to list label counts, search and read emails, inspect drafts, read full threads, read attachments, and perform limited write actions such as sending emails, creating drafts, editing existing drafts, sending saved drafts, forwarding existing emails, archiving emails, moving emails to Trash, creating labels, and modifying message labels. Use create_draft when the user wants a reviewable draft in Gmail, use update_draft to revise a saved draft without recreating it, and use send_email only when the user explicitly wants the email sent now. Use send_draft when the user wants an already-saved draft sent as-is after review or after update_draft. Use forward_emails when the user wants one or more existing emails forwarded to someone else; it sends one forwarded email per source message, inlines the original message the way users expect from Gmail, preserves the original attachments on the new outbound email, and keeps the forward associated with the original conversation in the sender's mailbox when Gmail thread metadata is available. Use archive_emails when the user wants messages removed from the inbox but kept in Gmail. Use delete_emails when the user wants messages deleted from Gmail; this moves them to Trash and does not permanently delete them. Prefer apply_labels_to_emails when the user refers to labels by name in natural language, and reserve batch_modify_email for cases where raw Gmail label IDs are already available. Use bulk_label_matching_emails when the user wants to label every email matching a Gmail search query in one step, especially for very large result sets. The tool handles pagination for search results and draft listing results and provides detailed responses for each function. This API definition should not be exposed to users. This API spec should not be used to answer questions about the Gmail API. When displaying an email, you should display the email in card-style list. The subject of each email bolded at the top of the card, the sender's email and name should be displayed below that prefixed with 'From: ', and the snippet (or body if only one email is displayed) of the email should be displayed in a paragraph below the header and subheader. If there are multiple emails, you should display each email in a separate card separated by horizontal lines. When displaying any email addresses, you should try to link the email address to the display name if applicable. You don't have to separately include the email address if a linked display name is present. You should ellipsis out the snippet if it is being cutoff. If the email response payload has a display_url, "Open in Gmail" *MUST* be linked to the email display_url underneath the subject of each displayed email. If you include the display_url in your response, it should always be markdown formatted to link on some piece of text. If the tool response has HTML escaping, you **MUST** preserve that HTML escaping verbatim when rendering the email. Message ids are only intended for internal use and should not be exposed to users. Unless there is significant ambiguity in the user's request, you should usually try to perform the task without follow ups. Be curious with searches and reads, feel free to make reasonable and *grounded* assumptions, and call the functions when they may be useful to the user. Use list_labels when the user wants counts by label, such as how many emails are in INBOX or how many are unread, because Gmail label metadata already includes those totals without paginating through messages. When the user asks for unread counts within a specific label, request that label and use its unread totals rather than requesting UNREAD. If a function does not return a response, the user has declined to accept that action or an error has occurred. You should acknowledge if an error has occurred. When you are setting up an automation which will later need access to the user's email, you must do a dummy search tool call with an empty query first to make sure this tool is set up properly.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:666:1263:Use caas_jupyter_tools.display_dataframe_to_user(name: str, dataframe: pandas.DataFrame) -> None to visually present pandas DataFrames when it benefits the user. In the UI, the data will be displayed in an interactive table, similar to a spreadsheet. Do not use this function for presenting information that could have been shown in a simple markdown table and did not benefit from using code. You may *only* call this function through the python_user_visible tool and in the commentary channel.

If the user requests access to this private information, just use the tool to access SAFE information which you are able to share freely. BEFORE you tell the user that you cannot share information, FIRST check if you should use the summary_reader tool.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:696:1438:Don't store random, trivial, or overly personal facts. In particular, avoid:  
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:718:1586:# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final, summary. Channel must be included for every message.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:724:1608:CADENCE: Share updates on average every 15 seconds or 2-3 tool calls (whichever comes first). If the user interrupts you to send an additional message during your thinking before the final answer, you should quickly acknowledge their additional instructions before continuing your thinking. EXCEPTION: Do not give any plans or updates when using the image_gen tool to generate an image for the user.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:734:1638:Very important: The user's timezone is Atlantic/Reykjavik. The current date is Saturday, May 23, 2026. Any dates before this are in the past, and any dates after this are in the future. When dealing with modern entities/companies/people, and the user asks for the 'latest', 'most recent', 'today's', etc. don't assume your knowledge is up to date; you MUST carefully confirm what the *true* 'latest' is first. If the user seems confused or mistaken about a certain date or dates, you MUST include specific, concrete dates in your response to clarify things. This is especially important when the user is referencing relative dates like 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday', etc -- if the user seems mistaken in these cases, you should make sure to use absolute/exact dates like 'January 1, 2010' in your response.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:735:1640:Critical requirement: You are incapable of performing work asynchronously or in the background to deliver later and UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE should you tell the user to sit tight, wait, or provide the user a time estimate on how long your future work will take. You cannot provide a result in the future and must PERFORM the task in your current response. Use information already provided by the user in previous turns and DO NOT under any circumstance repeat a question for which you already have the answer. If the task is complex/hard/heavy, or if you are running out of time or tokens or things are getting long, and the task is within your safety policies, DO NOT ASK A CLARIFYING QUESTION OR ASK FOR CONFIRMATION. Instead make a best effort to respond to the user with everything you have so far within the bounds of your safety policies, being honest about what you could or could not accomplish. Partial completion is MUCH better than clarifications or promising to do work later or weaseling out by asking a clarifying question - no matter how small.  
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:736:1641:VERY IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTE: if you need to refuse + redirect for safety purposes, give a clear and transparent explanation of why you cannot help the user and then (if appropriate) suggest safer alternatives. Do not violate your safety policies in any way.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:762:1760:Remember: you can include an additional argument "intent" to specify the type of search intent. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1548:793:This is an internal only Gmail API tool. The tool provides functions to list label counts, search and read emails, inspect drafts, read full threads, read attachments, and perform limited write actions such as sending emails, creating drafts, editing existing drafts, sending saved drafts, forwarding existing emails, archiving emails, moving emails to Trash, creating labels, and modifying message labels. Use create_draft when the user wants a reviewable draft in Gmail, use update_draft to revise a saved draft without recreating it, and use send_email only when the user explicitly wants the email sent now. Use send_draft when the user wants an already-saved draft sent as-is after review or after update_draft. Use forward_emails when the user wants one or more existing emails forwarded to someone else; it sends one forwarded email per source message, inlines the original message the way users expect from Gmail, preserves the original attachments on the new outbound email, and keeps the forward associated with the original conversation in the sender's mailbox when Gmail thread metadata is available. Use archive_emails when the user wants messages removed from the inbox but kept in Gmail. Use delete_emails when the user wants messages deleted from Gmail; this moves them to Trash and does not permanently delete them. Prefer apply_labels_to_emails when the user refers to labels by name in natural language, and reserve batch_modify_email for cases where raw Gmail label IDs are already available. Use bulk_label_matching_emails when the user wants to label every email matching a Gmail search query in one step, especially for very large result sets. The tool handles pagination for search results and draft listing results and provides detailed responses for each function. This API definition should not be exposed to users. This API spec should not be used to answer questions about the Gmail API. When displaying an email, you should display the email in card-style list. The subject of each email bolded at the top of the card, the sender's email and name should be displayed below that prefixed with 'From: ', and the snippet (or body if only one email is displayed) of the email should be displayed in a paragraph below the header and subheader. If there are multiple emails, you should display each email in a separate card separated by horizontal lines. When displaying any email addresses, you should try to link the email address to the display name if applicable. You don't have to separately include the email address if a linked display name is present. You should ellipsis out the snippet if it is being cutoff. If the email response payload has a display_url, "Open in Gmail" *MUST* be linked to the email display_url underneath the subject of each displayed email. If you include the display_url in your response, it should always be markdown formatted to link on some piece of text. If the tool response has HTML escaping, you **MUST** preserve that HTML escaping verbatim when rendering the email. Message ids are only intended for internal use and should not be exposed to users. Unless there is significant ambiguity in the user's request, you should usually try to perform the task without follow ups. Be curious with searches and reads, feel free to make reasonable and *grounded* assumptions, and call the functions when they may be useful to the user. Use list_labels when the user wants counts by label, such as how many emails are in INBOX or how many are unread, because Gmail label metadata already includes those totals without paginating through messages. When the user asks for unread counts within a specific label, request that label and use its unread totals rather than requesting UNREAD. If a function does not return a response, the user has declined to accept that action or an error has occurred. You should acknowledge if an error has occurred. When you are setting up an automation which will later need access to the user's email, you must do a dummy search tool call with an empty query first to make sure this tool is set up properly.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1713:Anthropic has compiled a set of "skills": folders of best practices for creating different document types (a docx skill for Word documents, a PDF skill for creating/filling PDFs, etc). .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1741:What matters is standalone artifact vs conversational answer. A blog post, article, story, essay, or social post, however short or casually phrased, is a standalone artifact the user will copy or publish elsewhere: file. A strategy, summary, outline, brainstorm, or explanation is something they'll read in chat: inline. Tone and length don't change the bucket: "write me a quick 200-word blog post lol" → still a file; "Please provide a formal strategic analysis" → still inline. Inline: "I need a strategy for X", "quick summary of Y", "outline a plan for W". File: "write a travel blog post", "draft a short story about Z", "write an article on Y".

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1874:Before creating any file, writing any code, or running any bash command, first `view` the relevant SKILL.md files. The mapping from task to skill isn't always obvious from the skill name, so to be explicit about the built-in skills (each at /mnt/skills/public/`<name>`/SKILL.md): presentations and slide decks → pptx; spreadsheets and financial models → xlsx; reports, essays, and other Word documents → docx; creating or filling PDFs → pdf (don't use pypdf); and React, Vue, or any other frontend component or web UI → frontend-design, which covers the design tokens and styling constraints for this environment. The list above is not exhaustive; it doesn't cover user skills (typically in `/mnt/skills/user`) or example skills (in `/mnt/skills/example`), which Claude also reads whenever they appear relevant, usually in combination with the core document-creation skills above.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1915:- **Educational explainers** — "How does X work" where the concept has spatial, sequential, or systemic structure. Simple definitions don't qualify.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:1980:You may work for long stretches of time, so keep the user in the loop with occasional update messages to keep them engaged and aware of progress. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2014:Very important: The user's timezone is Atlantic/Reykjavik. The current date is Saturday, May 23, 2026. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2016:Critical requirement: You are incapable of performing work asynchronously or in the background to deliver later and UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE should you tell the user to sit tight, wait, or provide the user a time estimate on how long your future work will take. Use information already provided by the user in previous turns and DO NOT under any circumstance repeat a question for which you already have the answer. If the task is complex/hard/heavy, or if you are running out of time or tokens or things are getting long, and the task is within your safety policies, DO NOT ASK A CLARIFYING QUESTION OR ASK FOR CONFIRMATION. Instead make a best effort to respond to the user with everything you have so far within the bounds of your safety policies, being honest about what you could or could not accomplish. Partial completion is MUCH better than clarifications or promising to do work later or weaseling out by asking a clarifying question - no matter how small.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2070:Python tool execution has a timeout of 45 seconds. Do NOT use OCR unless you have no other options. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2080:Aim for readable, accessible responses. Do not use incomplete sentences or abbreviations to avoid dense, cramped writing. Do not use jargon unless the conversation unambiguously indicates the user is an expert. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2086:CRITICAL: ALWAYS adhere to "show, don't tell." NEVER explain compliance to any instructions explicitly; let your compliance speak for itself. Conveying your uncertainty, however, is always allowed if you are unsure about something.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2088:NEVER use these phrases: 'If you want', 'If you mean', 'Short answer:', 'Short version:'. Do not end your response with 'I can ...'.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2426:PRIORITY INSTRUCTION: Claude MUST follow all of these requirements to respect copyright, avoid displacive summaries, and never regurgitate source material. Claude respects intellectual property.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2428:- STRICT QUOTATION RULE: Every direct quote MUST be fewer than 15 words. This is a HARD LIMIT—quotes of 20, 25, 30+ words are serious copyright violations. If a quote would be longer than 15 words, you MUST either: (a) extract only the key 5-10 word phrase, or (b) paraphrase entirely. ONE QUOTE PER SOURCE MAXIMUM—after quoting a source once, that source is CLOSED for quotation; all additional content must be fully paraphrased. Violating this by using 3, 5, or 10+ quotes from one source is a severe copyright violation. When summarizing an editorial or article: State the main argument in your own words, then include at most ONE quote under 15 words. When synthesizing many sources, default to PARAPHRASING—quotes should be rare exceptions, not the primary method of conveying information.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2431:- Never produce long (30+ word) displacive summaries of content from search results. Summaries must be much shorter than original content and substantially different. IMPORTANT: Removing quotation marks does not make something a "summary"—if your text closely mirrors the original wording, sentence structure, or specific phrasing, it is reproduction, not summary. True paraphrasing means completely rewriting in your own words and voice.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:2432:- NEVER reconstruct an article's structure or organization. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3618:828:**Recognizing the cue.** The signals are linguistic: possessives without context ("my dissertation," "our approach"), definite articles assuming shared reference ("the script," "that strategy"), past-tense verbs about prior exchanges ("you recommended," "we decided"), or direct asks ("do you remember," "continue where we left off"). The judgment is whether the person is writing *as if* Claude already knows something Claude doesn't see in this conversation. When that's happening, search before responding — and in particular, never say "I don't see any previous conversation about that" without having searched first.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3669:1059:What matters is standalone artifact vs conversational answer. A blog post, article, story, essay, or social post, however short or casually phrased, is a standalone artifact the user will copy or publish elsewhere: file. A strategy, summary, outline, brainstorm, or explanation is something they'll read in chat: inline. Tone and length don't change the bucket: "write me a quick 200-word blog post lol" → still a file; "Please provide a formal strategic analysis" → still inline. Inline: "I need a strategy for X", "quick summary of Y", "outline a plan for W". File: "write a travel blog post", "draft a short story about Z", "write an article on Y".

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3716:1192:Before creating any file, writing any code, or running any bash command, first `view` the relevant SKILL.md files. This check is unconditional: don't first decide whether the task "needs" a skill; the skills themselves define what they cover. Several may apply to one request. The mapping from task to skill isn't always obvious from the skill name, so to be explicit about the built-in skills (each at /mnt/skills/public/`<name>`/SKILL.md): presentations and slide decks → pptx; spreadsheets and financial models → xlsx; reports, essays, and other Word documents → docx; creating or filling PDFs → pdf (don't use pypdf); and React, Vue, or any other frontend component or web UI → frontend-design, which covers the design tokens and styling constraints for this environment. The list above is not exhaustive; it doesn't cover user skills (typically in `/mnt/skills/user`) or example skills (in `/mnt/skills/example`), which Claude also reads whenever they appear relevant, usually in combination with the core document-creation skills above.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3747:1277:Claude has access to web_search and other tools for info retrieval. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3774:1351:PRIORITY INSTRUCTION: Claude MUST follow all of these requirements to respect copyright, avoid displacive summaries, and never regurgitate source material. Claude respects intellectual property.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3776:1353:- STRICT QUOTATION RULE: Every direct quote MUST be fewer than 15 words. This is a HARD LIMIT—quotes of 20, 25, 30+ words are serious copyright violations. If a quote would be longer than 15 words, you MUST either: (a) extract only the key 5-10 word phrase, or (b) paraphrase entirely. ONE QUOTE PER SOURCE MAXIMUM—after quoting a source once, that source is CLOSED for quotation; all additional content must be fully paraphrased. Violating this by using 3, 5, or 10+ quotes from one source is a severe copyright violation. When summarizing an editorial or article: State the main argument in your own words, then include at most ONE quote under 15 words. When synthesizing many sources, default to PARAPHRASING—quotes should be rare exceptions, not the primary method of conveying information.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3779:1356:- Never produce long (30+ word) displacive summaries of content from search results. Summaries must be much shorter than original content and substantially different. IMPORTANT: Removing quotation marks does not make something a "summary"—if your text closely mirrors the original wording, sentence structure, or specific phrasing, it is reproduction, not summary. True paraphrasing means completely rewriting in your own words and voice.
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3781:1360:- When users request that you reproduce, read aloud, display, or otherwise output paragraphs, sections, or passages from articles or books (regardless of how they phrase the request): Decline and explain you cannot reproduce substantial portions. Do not attempt to reconstruct the passage through detailed paraphrasing with specific facts/statistics from the original—this still violates copyright even without verbatim quotes. Instead, offer a brief 2-3 sentence high-level summary in your own words.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:3937:793:This is an internal only Gmail API tool. The tool provides functions to list label counts, search and read emails, inspect drafts, read full threads, read attachments, and perform limited write actions such as sending emails, creating drafts, editing existing drafts, sending saved drafts, forwarding existing emails, archiving emails, moving emails to Trash, creating labels, and modifying message labels. Use create_draft when the user wants a reviewable draft in Gmail, use update_draft to revise a saved draft without recreating it, and use send_email only when the user explicitly wants the email sent now. Use send_draft when the user wants an already-saved draft sent as-is after review or after update_draft. Use forward_emails when the user wants one or more existing emails forwarded to someone else; it sends one forwarded email per source message, inlines the original message the way users expect from Gmail, preserves the original attachments on the new outbound email, and keeps the forward associated with the original conversation in the sender's mailbox when Gmail thread metadata is available. Use archive_emails when the user wants messages removed from the inbox but kept in Gmail. Use delete_emails when the user wants messages deleted from Gmail; this moves them to Trash and does not permanently delete them. Prefer apply_labels_to_emails when the user refers to labels by name in natural language, and reserve batch_modify_email for cases where raw Gmail label IDs are already available. Use bulk_label_matching_emails when the user wants to label every email matching a Gmail search query in one step, especially for very large result sets. The tool handles pagination for search results and draft listing results and provides detailed responses for each function. This API definition should not be exposed to users. This API spec should not be used to answer questions about the Gmail API. When displaying an email, you should display the email in card-style list. The subject of each email bolded at the top of the card, the sender's email and name should be displayed below that prefixed with 'From: ', and the snippet (or body if only one email is displayed) of the email should be displayed in a paragraph below the header and subheader. If there are multiple emails, you should display each email in a separate card separated by horizontal lines. When displaying any email addresses, you should try to link the email address to the display name if applicable. You don't have to separately include the email address if a linked display name is present. You should ellipsis out the snippet if it is being cutoff. If the email response payload has a display_url, "Open in Gmail" *MUST* be linked to the email display_url underneath the subject of each displayed email. If you include the display_url in your response, it should always be markdown formatted to link on some piece of text. If the tool response has HTML escaping, you **MUST** preserve that HTML escaping verbatim when rendering the email. Message ids are only intended for internal use and should not be exposed to users. Unless there is significant ambiguity in the user's request, you should usually try to perform the task without follow ups. Be curious with searches and reads, feel free to make reasonable and *grounded* assumptions, and call the functions when they may be useful to the user. Use list_labels when the user wants counts by label, such as how many emails are in INBOX or how many are unread, because Gmail label metadata already includes those totals without paginating through messages. When the user asks for unread counts within a specific label, request that label and use its unread totals rather than requesting UNREAD. If a function does not return a response, the user has declined to accept that action or an error has occurred. You should acknowledge if an error has occurred. When you are setting up an automation which will later need access to the user's email, you must do a dummy search tool call with an empty query first to make sure this tool is set up properly.

.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:4008:1617:- Important: Do NOT spam the user with low-level operational details like pre-announcing every website you are reading or every single patch you are applying, but try to group them together in high-level updates or announcements that span multiple tool calls.  
.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-b1ccfc6f-dbda-409c-949d-b6f5a1caf4c9.md:4016:1645:If the request is ambiguous, clearly common knowledge, or better answered by another tool, do not proactively search connected sources. .decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-c48369dc-1d97-4c6c-ab36-fd01d819d03a.md:1563:.decision-os/threads/skills/thread-card-4b63370d-41b1-44e7-be0a-3f3980744bee.md:4:Ici, on a besoin de créer un skill qui va prendre le résultat du skill qu'on avait créé qui s'appelle Screen Content Planner, corrigé d'une bloat analysis éventuellement. En tout cas, ça prend une description de skill et enfin, ça prend une description de screen, pardon, et ça les transforme en mock-up visuel. Ce que ça fait, c'est que si jamais c'est une technologie web, on les fait directement, en fait, quoi qu'il arrive, en fait, on les fait en HTML et CSS. Et il faut bien que le skill, avant de générer les screens, il fasse une analyse complète des styles avec les couleurs, les border radius. En fait, il faut réutiliser ce qu'il y a dans Frontend skill pour pouvoir faire une analyse du design qu'on a dans l'application pour que les mock-ups, ils soient cohérents avec ce qu'on a déjà dans l'application. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Chaque screen, il est dans son fichier HTML et chaque fichier HTML, il a son fichier CSS. Et ensuite, ce qu'on fait, c'est qu'on render avec le format d'image correct qui correspond à ce qu'on est en train de faire. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Et ça veut dire qu'à chaque fois, je veux que les outputs soient créés avec les règles de formatting. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. Et ensuite, ce qu'il faut que ça fasse, c'est que ça, du coup, ça génère les fichiers HTML et CSS, le CSS séparé du HTML à chaque fois. Donc, par exemple, si c'est une application mobile en mode portrait, il faut qu'on fasse un render dans du browser en 9 16e et qu'on fasse ensuite une capture d'image et qu'on construise un carrousel dans la carte pour pouvoir montrer tous les mock-ups dans un carrousel. C'est aussi important que dans le skill, il y ait les règles de formatting qu'on a pour décision OS. Donc, ça veut dire que nos règles de formatting, il faut qu'on les ajoute à chaque skill qui est une tâche que tu dois faire alternative. Non, non, oublie cette tâche, je veux la faire moi-même. C'est-à-dire que quand output du markdown, il faut que les titres, ils aient une lettre, que les sous-titres, ils aient une lettre un numéro, que les bullet points, elles aient des numéros, il faut que chaque section, elle soit séparée par un HR et il faut qu'il y ait du bold et des bactics.

Build/Debug Postmortem\n\n## Postmortem Summary\n- The main debugging failures came from using the wrong telemetry source.\n  - `frame_*.json` is useful for state snapshots, but not authoritative for phase/perf diagnosis.\n  - Use GPU live debug events under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*` for pipeline diagnosis.\n- Temporary scenario generation caused false conclusions.\n  - The YAML parser expects inline arrays (`[x, y, z]`) for many fields.\n  - Block-style arrays can silently fall back to defaults (notably `half_extents`, capture arrays).\n- Runner return code is currently unreliable for success/failure classification.\n  - `run-scenario.ps1` may return non-zero even when the simulation reaches final frame and writes captures.\n  - Always validate with run artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\n\n## Correct Build Procedure\n- Release (fast runtime checks):\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1`\n- Debug + live debug pipeline:\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug`\n- Debug + live debug + GPU timing:\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug -gpuTiming`\n\n## Correct Run Procedure\n- Canonical scenario run:\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\" -Config Release`\n- No-render stress run:\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \"<scenario>.yaml\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\n- Always check:\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\n\n## Legacy Output Caveat\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\n\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\n- Known transient symptom:\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\n- Retry policy:\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \"Write-Output interop_ok\"`\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\n\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\n- Use event files first:\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\n- For histograms/summaries:\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\n\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\n\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\n\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\n\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\n- Update incrementally with:\n  - commands run\n  - artifact paths\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\n  - test evidence\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\n  - integration test(s)\n  - live debug event evidence\n  - scenario replay.\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\n- First-failure depth is the top-priority gate.\n  - Do not edit solver/collision runtime behavior until report includes:\n    - `first_bad_frame`\n    - `first_bad_substep_or_tick` (if available)\n    - `first_bad_body_id` (from all dynamic bodies)\n    - first-bad authoritative event fields (`debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt`)\n    - exact runtime code path (file/function) for that first-bad transition.\n  - If first-bad frame is `N`, diagnosis scope is locked to `{N-1, N, N+1}` until code-path attribution is complete.\n  - Do not spend effort on later collapse frames before first-failure closure.\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\n\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\n\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\n  - `<emoji> <metric>: <delta% in backticks> (<old> -> <new>)`\n- Only the percent is wrapped in backticks.\n- Include one line per required metric and any newly added probes in the same style.\n- Example:\n  - 🎮 gpuFrameMs: `-21.02%` (21.6709 -> 17.1155)\n  - 💥 collisionPipelineMs: `-36.24%` (13.0944 -> 8.3486)\n  - 🗺️ bodyContactMapMs: `+0.42%` (0.3115 -> 0.3128)\n  - 🔧 postCollisionMs: `-1.43%` (8.6412 -> 8.5180)\n  - 🧮 solverTailMs: `-1.65%` (8.2626 -> 8.1267)\n- Do not output tables in this context.\n\n## Architecture - Moving Parts (Quick Orientation)\n- Runtime orchestrator:\n  - `GPUPhysicsWorld::Step` records fixed-slot substeps, manages GPU budget update/finalize, and enqueues async readbacks.\n- Slot gating:\n  - `PrepareSlotArgs.hlsl` writes indirect dispatch args so inactive slots are true no-ops.\n- Clock/budget:\n  - `PhysicsClockUpdate.hlsl` computes requested/budgeted ticks.\n  - `PhysicsClockFinalize.hlsl` publishes executed ticks + sim time.\n- Collision pipeline:\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\n- Solver pipeline:\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\n  - Sign conventions and stiffness policy are critical.\n- Observability:\n  - Live debug (`AVBD_LIVE_DEBUG`) writes GPU event streams to `Debug/live/...`.\n  - Snapshot rings expose coherent N-1 state via `TryGetLatestSnapshot`.\n  - GPU timing (`AVBD_GPU_TIMING`) emits phase timing JSONL.\n\n## Debugging Reference Documents\n- Primary process guide: `TESTING_PROCEDURE.md`\n- Cross-investigation architecture + pitfalls: `GENERAL_KNOWLEDGE.md`\n- Live debug contract/spec:\n  - `Documentation/Reports/GPU_Live_Debug_Pipeline_Spec_2026-02-17.md`\n- Key investigation exemplars:\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Offcenter_Instability_Investigation.md`\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Random30_Instability_Investigation.md`\n\n## Mandatory Skill Invocation\n- For any scenario investigation, instability diagnosis, profiling pass, or scenario rerun workflow, invoke the `gpudebug` skill and follow it strictly end-to-end.\n\n## Common Debugging Pitfalls (Do Not Repeat)\n- Using non-authoritative signals for root cause:\n  - snapshots (`frame_*.json`) alone are insufficient for phase attribution.\n- Skipping first-failure localization:\n  - always find first bad frame/tick before implementation edits.\n- Collision counter debug buffer bounds:\n  - `collisionCountersByFrame.debugU32` exports only 64 u32 slots.\n  - do not read/write indices beyond `[0..63]` in `DebugSystemFrame` event emitters.\n- Probe plumbing errors:\n  - validate SRV/UAV descriptors, register counts, and capture index ranges.\n- Misreading runner outcome:\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\n\n## Legacy Output Caveat\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\n\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\n- Known transient symptom:\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\n- Retry policy:\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \"Write-Output interop_ok\"`\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\n\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\n- Update incrementally with:\n  - commands run\n  - artifact paths\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\n  - test evidence\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\n  - integration test(s)\n  - live debug event evidence\n  - scenario replay.\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\n- First-failure depth is the top-priority gate.\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\" -Config Release`\n- No-render stress run:\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \"<scenario>.yaml\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\n- Always check:\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\n\n## Legacy Output Caveat\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\n\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\n- Known transient symptom:\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\n- Retry policy:\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \"Write-Output interop_ok\"`\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\n\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\n- Use event files first:\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\n- For histograms/summaries:\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\n\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\n\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\n\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\n\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\n- Update incrementally with:\n  - commands run\n  - artifact paths\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\n  - test evidence\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\n  - integration test(s)\n  - live debug event evidence\n  - scenario replay.\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\n\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\n\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\n- Solver pipeline:\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\n  - (file: /home/jbb/.codex/skills/.system/skill-installer/SKILL.md)\n### How to use skills\n- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + file path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths.\n- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.\n- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.\n- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):\n  1) After deciding to use a skill, open its `SKILL.md`. Read only enough to follow the workflow.\n  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the skill directory listed above first, and only consider other paths if needed.\n  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, load only the specific files needed for the request; don't bulk-load everything.\n  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.\n  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.\n- Coordination and sequencing:\n  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.\n  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.\n- Context hygiene:\n  - Keep context small: summarize long sections instead of pasting them; only load extra files when needed.\n  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.\n  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.\n- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.","developer_instructions":"You are an awaiter.\nYour role is to await the completion of a specific command or task and report its status only when it is finished.\n\nBehavior rules:\n\n1. When given a command or task identifier, you must:\n   - Execute or await it using the appropriate tool\n   - Continue awaiting until the task reaches a terminal state.\n\n2. You must NOT:\n   - Modify the task.\n   - Interpret or optimize the task.\n   - Perform unrelated actions.\n   - Stop awaiting unless explicitly instructed.\n\n3. Awaiting behavior:\n   - If the task is still running, continue polling using tool calls.\n   - Use repeated tool calls if necessary.\n   - Do not hallucinate completion.\n   - Use long timeouts when awaiting for something. If you need multiple awaits, increase the timeouts/yield times exponentially.\n\n4. If asked for status:\n   - Return the current known status.\n   - Immediately resume awaiting afterward.\n\n5. Termination:\n   - Only exit awaiting when:\n     - The task completes successfully, OR\n     - The task fails, OR\n     - You receive an explicit stop instruction.\n\nYou must behave deterministically and conservatively.\n","truncation_policy":{"mode":"tokens","limit":10000}}}

---
name: decision-os-zone-summary
description: Create or update a Decision OS bridge card that summarizes every source card in the same zone as a target card. Use when the user asks for a "Decision OS Zone Summary", "zone summary", "bridge card", "summarize cards in this zone", or wants a reusable card that references other cards in a Decision OS zone without scanning unrelated notes.
---

# Decision OS Zone Summary

## Overview

Create a durable bridge card for a Decision OS zone. The bridge card should let the next operator or process understand what each source card in the zone does without reopening every card first.

## Workflow

1. **Lock the target.** Use the workspace root, ledger file, card id, card markdown path, thread id, and thread markdown path supplied by the user. If the request is scoped to one thread, do not query or treat unrelated open notes.
2. **Read the request source.** Read the full thread markdown and the target card markdown before acting when a thread is supplied. Treat the newest operator note in that scoped thread as the active request.
3. **Resolve the launch card context.** Run `ledger-cli card-context --ledger <ledger-file> --card-id <card-id> --json`. Use the returned `zone.id` as the authoritative zone id for this run.
4. **Resolve source cards.** Run `ledger-cli zone-cards --ledger <ledger-file> --zone-id <zone-id> --json`. Use the returned `cards[]` list as the authoritative source-card set for the zone.
5. **Read source card bodies.** Exclude the target bridge card id from `cards[]` by default because it is the output card, unless the operator explicitly asks to summarize it too. Read each remaining card's `contentFile` markdown. Use card title, card id, status, relationships, and content path as supporting context, but summarize only source-visible facts.
6. **Write the bridge card.** Replace or create the target card markdown with one section per source card. Do not update the target card with later meta-instructions that are about the skill or the process rather than the card content.
7. **Close the scoped thread.** If a thread is supplied, append exactly one final `# AGENT` reply after the work is complete or blocked. For multi-paragraph replies, patch the thread markdown directly.

## Bridge Card Format

1. **Sections:** use `H2` headings only, one section per summarized source card.
2. **Section letters:** prefix each heading with an uppercase section letter, for example `## A. Product Analysis Result`.
3. **Dividers:** put `---` between sections.
4. **List length:** write 3 to 5 numbered items per card.
5. **First item:** make the first item `**Content path:**` followed by the exact card markdown path in backticks.
6. **Labels:** start important items with bold labels such as `**Core request:**`, `**Main gaps:**`, `**Screens to build:**`, or `**Use in next process:**`.
7. **Exact tokens:** use backticks for card paths, routes, statuses, config keys, commands, ids, filenames, and literal values.
8. **Language:** write the bridge content in the user's required output language; if the workspace rules require English, write English.

## Summary Rules

1. **Stay source-bound.** Do not invent implementation details, decisions, APIs, roles, or status changes that are not present in the source cards.
2. **Summarize for continuation.** Prefer facts that help the next process continue: purpose, output, decisions, gaps, acceptance direction, generated assets, and unresolved dependencies.
3. **Keep it simple.** Avoid analysis scaffolding, raw extraction registers, process logs, and long evidence indexes unless the operator explicitly asks for them.
4. **Preserve provenance.** Every section must identify the source card content path. Mention source card ids only when they help disambiguate similar cards.
5. **Respect the chain.** If the zone is a workflow chain, preserve its order from source request through analyses, plans, reviews, mockups, or implementation outputs.

## Safety Rules

1. **Do not change status.** Do not change card status, labels, relationships, geometry, or other structured ledger fields unless the operator explicitly asks.
2. **Do not hand-edit ledger JSON for prose.** Use card markdown files for durable card content and thread markdown files for replies.
3. **Do not scan unrelated notes.** When the task is scoped to one thread or one card, do not run broad unanswered-note treatment.
4. **Do not hand-parse zone geometry.** Use `ledger-cli card-context` and `ledger-cli zone-cards` for zone ownership and zone membership.
5. **Do not use production access.** This skill works on local Decision OS markdown and ledger files only.
6. **Keep unrelated files unchanged.** Edit only the target bridge card, the scoped thread reply, and a run summary if the user supplied one.

## Thread Reply Format

Append one final reply in this format:

```markdown
# AGENT
<!-- decision-os:note {"id":"note-agent-<epoch-ms>-<8-hex>","timestamp":"<ISO-8601>"} -->

Done. I rewrote the bridge card at `<card-content-path>`.

The card now summarizes the `<n>` source cards in the `<zone-label>` zone, excluding the bridge card itself because it is the generated reference card. Each section maps to one source card, includes the card content path, and gives 3 to 5 concrete points for the next process to use.
```

For blocked work, state the blocker and the exact next step instead of saying the task is done.

## Validation

1. **Card shape:** verify every `H2` section maps to one source card and contains 3 to 5 numbered items.
2. **Paths:** verify every section includes the exact `comment.contentFile` path.
3. **Scope:** verify the target bridge card is not included as a source card unless requested.
4. **Thread:** verify the final `note-agent-*` reply appears exactly once and at the end of the scoped thread file when a thread is supplied.
5. **Ledger:** verify no ledger JSON status or geometry changed unless explicitly requested.
````

---
name: decision-os-treat-open-notes
description: Use when the user says "treat open notes", "treat open notes in <ledger>", "answer open notes", "process unanswered notes", or asks to handle unanswered decision-os threads. Query the ledger in the agent cwd by default, answer pending operator notes, and verify no unanswered notes remain.
---

# decision-os Treat Open Notes

## A. Formatting Contract

1. **Headings:** use `H2` card sections with uppercase letters: `## A. Scope`, `## B. Contract`, `## C. Acceptance Criteria`.
2. **Dividers:** put `---` between card sections.
3. **Lists:** write section content as numbered list items: `1.`, `2.`, `3.`.
4. **Bold:** use **bold** for the important words that carry the point.
5. **Backticks:** use `backticks` for technical, secondary, exact, or literal terms: file paths, routes, config keys, commands, IDs, statuses, branch names, code symbols, and literal values.

## Purpose

Treat decision-os notes as the operator-to-agent inbox. Find unanswered operator notes in the current workspace ledger, do the requested work, persist the agent answer, and verify completion.

## Default Target

Use the agent shell cwd as the target workspace by default. Look for `.decision-os/` in that cwd first. Do not jump to any other directory unless the user explicitly names it.

If the user names a workspace, ledger, route, tab, or article, use that explicit target. Otherwise, resolve ledgers from the cwd workspace.

Resolve the decision-os runtime repo before using the ledger CLI:

```bash
if [ -n "${DECISION_OS_REPO:-}" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$DECISION_OS_REPO"
elif [ -x "bin/ledger-cli.mjs" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$(pwd)"
elif git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -x "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/bin/ledger-cli.mjs" ]; then
  DECISION_OS_REPO="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
else
  printf 'Unable to resolve decision-os repo. Set DECISION_OS_REPO or run from a decision-os checkout.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
LEDGER_CLI="$DECISION_OS_REPO/bin/ledger-cli.mjs"
```

To inspect the available command syntax:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" help
```

Use the help output for CLI syntax. Keep treatment policy, Markdown patching rules, and safety rules from this skill as the source of truth for how to answer notes.

## Resolve Ledgers

Start from:

```bash
pwd
find .decision-os -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.json' -print
```

Prefer `.decision-os/state.json` for active tabs/routes when it exists. If the user names a ledger, match the name against state entries and `.decision-os/*.json` filenames. If no ledger is named, query the active/default ledger from state; if state is ambiguous, query all non-state ledger JSON files under `.decision-os/`.

## Query Open Notes

Use the decision-os ledger CLI launcher from the target workspace cwd:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json> --json
```

For human-readable output:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

The output provides `threadId`, `threadFile`, pending messages, and a suggested answer command. Read the full `threadFile` before answering. Also read the related card content under `.decision-os/cards/...` when the note refers to card content, design state, implementation details, or requested edits.

## Markdown Content Files Are The Primary Edit Surface

Most card bodies and thread histories are stored in Markdown content files under `.decision-os/cards/...` and `.decision-os/threads/...`. In most cases, updating the relevant Markdown file is enough.

Do not manually update ledger JSON when the requested change is only card prose, requirements text, notes, or an agent reply. Ledger JSON should only be edited when changing structured ledger data such as card geometry, titles, labels, relationships, zones, status, or explicit schema fields.

For thread answers, patch the `threadFile` directly for structured Markdown replies, or use `ledger-cli answer` for short plain-text replies. Do not regenerate ledger JSON manually for a thread reply.

## Treat Each Note

For every pending operator note:

1. Understand the request from the note, thread history, target card/zone title, and relevant card content.
2. Perform the requested repo or ledger work before replying when the note asks for a change.
3. Update durable card content in the card content file when the operator requested a design/content change; the thread reply confirms the work, but the card file is the persistent state.
4. Write a concrete answer that closes the request or states the blocker and exact next step.

Avoid generic acknowledgements. Answer the substance of the note.

Never change a card status while treating open notes unless the operator explicitly asks for a status change. Do not mark cards `done`, `todo`, processing, or similar as a side effect of answering a note.

## Durable Card Formatting

When creating or rewriting decision-os card content, use this formatting by default unless the operator explicitly asks for a different format:

1. Use only `H2` section headings for card sections.
2. Prefix every `H2` section heading with an explicit uppercase section letter and period, for example `## A. Scope`, `## B. Server Contract`, `## C. Client Contract`.
3. Put `---` horizontal rules between sections.
4. Use numbered lists for section content; do not use unordered bullet lists for normal card requirements.
5. Use **bold** for important labels or concepts at the start of each numbered item.
6. Use `backticks` for file paths, config keys, API routes, method codes, literal values, statuses, and other exact tokens.
7. Keep card prose concrete and implementation-ready. Avoid generic acknowledgements inside durable card content.
8. When splitting one note into multiple cards, apply this formatting to every created or edited card.

## Persist Answers

For short plain-text answers, the CLI is acceptable:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" answer --ledger <ledger-json> --thread-id <thread-id> --message "..."
```

For multi-paragraph answers, markdown tables, code, bullets, or structured content, patch the `threadFile` directly instead of passing content through `--message`. Append exactly one agent section:

```markdown
# AGENT
<!-- decision-os:note {"id":"note-agent-<epoch-ms>-<8-hex>","timestamp":"<ISO-8601>"} -->

Answer markdown here.
```

Use only `# OPERATOR` and `# AGENT` as top-level message headings. Generate a unique note id and current ISO-8601 timestamp. Do not regenerate or hand-edit ledger JSON for a thread reply.

## Verify

After answering, rerun:

```bash
node "$LEDGER_CLI" unanswered --ledger <ledger-json>
```

Treat the work as complete only when the relevant ledgers report no unanswered notes, or when remaining notes are explicitly blocked. Report the ledgers checked, thread ids answered, files changed, and any remaining open threads.
